podcast.body: "Rocket 88" by Jackie Brenston is frequently referred to as the "canonical first rock and roll record," although the text posits that Wynonie Harris's "Good Rockin' Tonight" is an equally valid candidate and that rock and roll had already become a "cohesive unified whole" by 1948. "And while were still three years away, even from the canonical first rock and roll record, Jackie Brenstens rocket 88."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 7: "Good Rockin' Tonight" by Wynonie Harris

podcast.body: This song, featuring Ike Turner on vocals, was among the early rock and roll tracks emerging in the early 1950s. Its appearance was described as "a little frightening" and was dubbed "the devil's music" by some. It represented a blend of rhythm and blues (previously known as "race records") with hillbilly and country music, creating a "strange offspring" that scared "decent folks." "It was actually a little frightening."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
